resources.string: Yomira is not an official AniZen release. It builds on the work of the projects below, under the Apache 2.0 license.
Discord Rich Presence is off in this build. It needs a Discord application registered by whoever builds the app; Yomira does not reuse the one from AniZen.
Could not load the servers for this episode
This source offered no server for this episode
None of the servers returned a playable video
The video stopped or could not be opened
Links can expire. Try again, choose another server or pick another episode.
The downloaded file is not a valid APK. The repository may be serving a broken or incomplete file.
%1$s is not an anime extension (it does not declare tachiyomi.animeextension).
This extension uses extension library %1$s; Yomira supports versions %2$d to %3$d.
Version %1$s is installed and Android does not install an older version (%2$s) over it. Uninstall the extension first if you really want this version.

The installed copy of this extension was signed with a different key. Android cannot update between signatures: uninstall the current extension, then install this one. Its settings for this source will be lost.
Android refused the update because it conflicts with the installed package (usually a different signature).
Android says this APK is incompatible with the device (Android version or CPU architecture).
Not enough storage to install the extension.
The installation was blocked by the system. Allow Yomira to install unknown apps and try again.
The system installer could not install the extension.
Hidden: adult sources are turned off
Adult sources can be turned on in Settings → Browse.
Paste the address of a repository in the AniZen/Aniyomi legacy format (it ends with index.min.json). Any compatible repository works.
Suggested repositories are maintained by third parties, not by Yomira.
The repository could not be reached. Check the address and the network connection.
The address answered, but it is not a repository Yomira can read: it needs repo.json and index.min.json in the same folder.

This address is a store-v2 index, the format used by newer Aniyomi builds, which Yomira does not read. Use the index.min.json address of the same repository (for Rede: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lyraEz/Rede/repo/index.min.json).
This device does not have that settings screen.
No app on this device can open %1$s
Bulges the centre like a magnifying lens. Ultra only.
Rainbow fringe on small round buttons. Ultra only.
Live blur needs Android 12 and refraction needs Android 13. On older phones, or with quality Off, overlays are drawn as translucent surfaces with no extra cost.
Recommended for this phone: off. It does not have the headroom to run Anime4K without dropping frames.
For HD anime (720p/1080p) that looks blurry or blocky: cleans compression artefacts and sharpens the lines.
For HD anime with only light blur: a softer restore that keeps the original line art.
For low-resolution or noisy video (480p and below): removes noise and enlarges. The lightest mode.
A stronger A that restores twice. Heavy: flagship phones only.
A stronger B. Heavy: flagship phones only.
For very poor sources: removes noise, then restores. Heavy.
Fast uses the smallest network and costs almost nothing; High looks best but can drop frames on most phones.
Measuring for %1$d s… keep the video playing
Smooth: no dropped frames in %1$d s.
%1$d frames dropped and %2$d late in %3$d s. Switched to a lighter setting; check again.
%1$d frames dropped in %2$d s even at the lightest setting. Anime4K was turned off for smooth playback.
Safe mode is on: glass effects are off
It was turned on from the crash report. Tap to turn it off and restart the screen.
Asks the screen for a refresh rate that fits the video's frame rate (e.g. 24 fps on 120 Hz), removing judder at no cost. Android 11+.
Blends frames to the screen's refresh rate. Smoothest on 60 Hz screens; uses a little more GPU. Applies from the next video.
Simple scaling. Lightest on the GPU, never drops frames, slightly softer picture.
Sharp scaling with clean downscaling. Good picture at a small GPU cost.
Sharpest scaling (Lanczos) with smooth edges. Best picture; for strong phones.
Loads up to two minutes ahead so slow or unstable connections do not pause playback. Uses more memory. Applies from the next video.
How often the glass controls follow the video. 30 fps is smooth and light; Off turns the live glass off for maximum performance.
When the phone falls behind, frames are skipped early in the decoder so audio and video stay together instead of stuttering.
Lighter software decoding (skips the loop filter on non-reference frames). For phones without hardware decoding; tiny quality loss. Applies from the next video.
Jumps to the nearest keyframe instantly instead of the exact frame. Seeking feels immediate.
Shows dropped (VO, DEC) and late frames in the corner, to check that playback is smooth.
Softens the light halos sharp scaling leaves around lines and subtitles.
Dithering hides colour banding in skies and dark scenes at almost no cost.
Removes comb lines from interlaced DVD or broadcast sources. Leave off for normal anime.
How HDR video is fitted to the screen. Auto is best for most; Hable is punchier, Mobius keeps more colour.

Checks each new video and this phone and keeps everything at the video\'s own frame rate: the screen switches to that rate or an exact multiple when it can, and image quality and effects are chosen so no frames drop. On-device rules and measurements, no internet.
Waiting for the video to start…
Screen at %1$d Hz: every video frame stays exactly %2$d refreshes. Perfect cadence, no judder.
Screen at %1$d Hz: this phone has no exact multiple of this video, so the video keeps its own frame rate and the screen is left alone.
Battery saver or low battery: lighter plan until you charge.
✦ marks the recommendation: the video\'s own rate or the closest exact multiple the screen supports.
Video fps shows every frame at the episode\'s original timing (recommended). Locked fits the video to the screen; Locked + smooth also blends frames and costs more.
Chosen from the video\'s pixels per second and this phone\'s power.
Live glass on the controls costs a little GPU; lower on weaker phones.
Frames were dropping, so this video was adjusted automatically: %1$s.
Watches the dropped-frame counters while you watch and steps down one level at a time if the phone falls behind.
On battery saver or below 15%, uses a lighter plan.
Lets the screen change refresh rate even when the switch blanks it for a moment (Android 12+). Turn on if your phone ignores seamless switches.
Evens out loud and quiet parts: explosions stay calm and whispers stay audible.
Brings quiet speech up to a steady level.
A gentle low-end lift for phone speakers and earbuds.
After a pause longer than 30 seconds, goes back a few seconds so you do not lose the thread.
The phone is getting hot: switched the player to its lightest settings to avoid stutters.
Player settings restored to the light defaults. Some apply from the next video.
Mark where it starts and ends to watch a scene on repeat.
Repeating from %1$s; now mark the end.
Pauses and moves one frame at a time, for screenshots and details.
For videos recorded sideways. Back to 0° to undo.
Stop at the end of this episode
Does not start the next one this time, even with autoplay on.
Each anime opens at the last speed you used in it.
The same sound in both ears, for one earbud or hearing in one ear.
Mixes a little of each side into the other so the sound feels in front of you and tires less.
Lifts the highs of muffled audio.
Current time under the episode title.
Battery level, in red when it gets low.
When the episode ends at the current speed.
Warm tint over the video for watching at night.
Only time the video is actually playing counts. Everything stays on this phone.
A light tick when switching tabs.
Episodes you have not watched show only their number, without summary, and with a blurred image.
Long-press the app icon to go back to the last episode you opened.
TMDB gives episode names, descriptions, thumbnails and title logos in your language. AniSkip and Anime Skip give opening and ending times; they now work without tracking the anime.
Not set: names and thumbnails come only from the extension
Checks that TMDB accepts the key
TMDB rejected the key (v3 key or v4 read token)
Could not reach TMDB, check the connection
Episode list, player and start screen
Names and descriptions without a translation use the English ones
Finds the anime on AniList by its title
Title and thin progress bar at the bottom, big controls in the middle, pause screen
How far the side buttons sit from play, as a share of the screen width
What the buttons next to play do
\"-21:59\" instead of \"03:33 / 25:34\" (tap the time to switch)
Logo, episode and description while the video is paused
Seconds paused without touching the screen
From TMDB; without it the name shows in large letters
On the start screen, above the tab bar
Added to the extension\'s episode numbers. Example: -12 when its episode 13 is the first of the season.
Add a TMDB key in Settings → Player → Metadata and skipping.
